sources.title: Martine Queffelec, Diophantine approximation and expansions of real numbers
sources.locator: §2 p215 and Definition3.1 p217; web lines17–24,72–83
sources.summary: Uses nonexact rational approximants and defines the irrationality exponent for irrational reals as a supremum over approximation orders. This supports varying the cutoff and retaining exact-error conventions carefully.

sources.title: Jon Aaronson and Hitoshi Nakada, Extravagance, irrationality and Diophantine approximation
sources.summary: Studies Diophantine and Liouville behavior for invariant measures and examples with arbitrary irrationality exponent. Generic cutoff statements therefore serve more than the algebraic Roth application.
